This technology has found applications in various fields, including education, healthcare, gaming, and retail. For instance, in education, AR can transform traditional learning experiences by providing interactive 3D models of complex subjects, making it easier for students to grasp challenging concepts. In retail, AR applications enable customers to visualize how products will look in their own homes or on their bodies before making a purchase. Despite its numerous advantages, challenges such as privacy concerns, the need for advanced hardware, and user adaptation remain obstacles to widespread adoption. As AR continues to evolve, its potential to revolutionize industries and enhance everyday activities grows.
